This vignette covers the two things people ask for first: how to reproduce the
visualizations published in the dbVisuals Application Note, and how to start each
of the package's entry points.

## Install

Everything comes from CRAN.

```{r}
install.packages(c("DBI", "duckdb", "rDeckgl", "rMosaic"))

# or let the package do it
dbVisuals::install_dbvisuals_deps()
```

`dbVisuals` itself is not on CRAN yet:

```{r}
remotes::install_github("dbverse-org/dbVisuals2", subdir = "r-package")
```

## Entry point 1 — the SQLRooms browser workspace

`launchBrowser()` starts a local server plus the packaged front end and opens a
browser. Point it at a DuckDB file, or omit `db_path` for an empty in-memory
database you can populate from the UI.

```{r}
library(dbVisuals)

# empty in-memory database
launchBrowser()

# an existing DuckDB / GiottoDB file
launchBrowser(db_path = "WTA_Preview_FFPE_Breast_Cancer_xenium.duckdb")

# non-blocking, so the R session stays usable
launchBrowser(db_path = "my.duckdb", daemon = TRUE)

stop_sqlrooms()
```

Ports default to 3001 (server) and 5173 (front end); pass `port` and
`frontend_port` to run several instances at once.

Push a data frame from R into the running workspace:

```{r}
# a data frame -> a table in the project database
sqlrooms_export_table("cars", mtcars)

# a lazy dbplyr pipeline -> a view, without pulling it into R
dplyr::tbl(con, "gdb_cell_metadata") |>
  dplyr::filter(x > 0) |>
  sqlrooms_register("cells_pos", x = _)
```

## Entry point 2 — R-side linked views with `mosaic_gl()`

`mosaic_gl()` is an htmlwidget: Mosaic views and GPU deck.gl layers in one
browser scope, over a single DuckDB-WASM coordinator and a single shared
selection, so brushing any panel filters all of them. No server, no browser
workspace — it renders in the RStudio viewer, a knitted document, or Shiny.

A self-contained example that needs no database:

```{r}
library(dbVisuals)

pts <- data.frame(x = rnorm(5000), y = rnorm(5000))

spec <- mgl_spec(
  data = list(pts = mgl_data(type = "table", df = pts)),
  plot = list(
    list(mark = "dot", data = list(from = "pts"), x = "x", y = "y"),
    mgl_deckgl(
      id     = "map",
      layers = list(list(
        type = "scatterplot", data = list(from = "pts"),
        x = "x", y = "y", radius = 3
      ))
    )
  ),
  width = 800, height = 500
)

mosaic_gl(spec)
```

Data reaches the browser as Arrow IPC, not JSON. `mgl_data(type = "table")`
serializes a data frame; `mgl_data(type = "duckdb", query = ...)` keeps the data
in the database and ships only the query result, which is what you want for
anything large:

```{r}
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "my.duckdb", read_only = TRUE)

spec <- mgl_spec(
  data = list(
    cells = mgl_data(type = "duckdb",
                     query = "SELECT x, y, leiden_clus FROM gdb_cell_metadata"),
    polys = mgl_data(type = "duckdb",
                     query = "SELECT ST_AsWKB(geom) AS geom FROM gdb_cell_polygons",
                     format = "geoarrow")
  ),
  plot = list(mgl_deckgl(id = "insitu", layers = list(
    list(type = "polygon",     data = list(from = "polys"), geometry = "geom"),
    list(type = "scatterplot", data = list(from = "cells"), x = "x", y = "y")
  )))
)

mosaic_gl(spec, con = con)
```

Passing `con` also lets the widget issue follow-up queries against your R-side
DuckDB while you interact, instead of materializing everything up front. Any
spatial / nanoarrow / geoarrow extensions already loaded on that connection are
reused.

In Shiny use the pair `mosaic_glOutput()` / `renderMosaic_gl()`.

## Entry point 3 — export a spec back out

Specs built in the browser workspace can be pulled back into R as an htmlwidget
for `rMosaic` or `rDeckgl`:

```{r}
dbvisuals_export_htmlwidget(spec, output = "panel.html")
```

## Reproducing the published figures

The in-situ panels come from `examples/` in this package. They need a GiottoDB
DuckDB database holding cell polygons, cell centroids and transcript
coordinates — the Application Note uses the 10x Genomics Atera In Situ Gene
Expression, FFPE Human Breast Cancer preview dataset on the Xenium platform.

| Script | Renders |
| --- | --- |
| `01_in_situ_with_marginals.R` | in-situ deck.gl view with linked Mosaic marginal histograms and a table |
| `02_in_situ_zoom_overlay.R` | full-tissue view with a region-of-interest zoom inset |
| `03_dimred_concat.R` | UMAP / PCA dimension pairs linked to a `leiden_clus` bar |
| `04_in_situ_with_transcripts.R` | cell polygons, centroids and subcellular transcripts |
| `05_in_situ_zoom_overlay_transcripts.R` | static ROI zoom inset with transcripts |
| `06_in_situ_zoom_overlay_transcripts_interactive.R` | **the published panel** — interactive ROI selection |

`03_dimred_concat.R` is the one that needs no database: it loads the Giotto mini
Visium object from `GiottoData`, so it is the quickest way to check the install.

`examples/` is not installed with the package (it is `.Rbuildignore`d, since the
scripts need data that does not ship), so run them from a clone of the
repository with `r-package/` as the working directory:

```r
setwd("path/to/dbVisuals2/r-package")
source("examples/03_dimred_concat.R")
```

For the in-situ scripts, point the environment at your data and run them from an
interactive session:

```r
setwd("path/to/dbVisuals2/r-package")
Sys.setenv(DBLENS_DEMO_DB = "/path/to/WTA_Preview_FFPE_Breast_Cancer_xenium.duckdb")
Sys.setenv(DBLENS_TRANSCRIPT_FILE = "/path/to/transcripts.parquet")  # 04, 05, 06 only
source("examples/06_in_situ_zoom_overlay_transcripts_interactive.R")
```

Neither variable is required to be set if the files sit in the working directory
under their default names. Optional overrides: `DBLENS_TRANSCRIPT_TABLE` to read
transcripts from a table inside the database instead of a file, and
`DBLENS_ROI_CELL_ID` to centre the region of interest on a specific cell.

Only script 06 is interactive: it starts a Shiny app where dragging the `select`
control re-queries just the transcripts inside the chosen region, and `detail`
picks the nested sub-region. Run it from an interactive R session — under
`Rscript` it prints the widget instead of launching Shiny. The published panel is
a full-window capture of the resulting three-view layout.

## Rebuilding the widget bundle

The pre-built browser bundle ships in `inst/htmlwidgets/`, so none of the above
needs `npm`. To rebuild it from source:

```bash
cd inst/viewer-src
npm install
npm run build
```

Versions of deck.gl, Mosaic, GeoArrow and Arrow are held to one contract across
this package and the front end; see `COMPATIBILITY.md` and `versions.json` at the
repository root, checked by `npm run test:versions`.
